edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice 4e, Modifiability ch., 'Reduce Coupling' tactics
edges.note: Reduce-coupling siblings: interpose a mediator vs. hide internals behind an explicit interface.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Modifiability ch., 'Reduce Coupling' tactics
edges.note: Both cut coupling: forbid a dependency outright vs. route it through an intermediary.
Factoring similar services into one general service hides the variant specifics behind a common interface.
Both shrink an element's interaction surface — runtime communication partners vs. module-level dependencies.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Integrability ch., 'Limit Dependencies' tactics
edges.note: Limit-dependencies siblings: forbid direct communication vs. route it through an intermediary.
Cohesion restructuring: split a non-cohesive module, then move related responsibilities together into one module.
Splitting an over-large module into cohesive pieces reduces the structural complexity that hampers testing.
Both gather scattered similar functionality into one place to cut duplication — move responsibilities vs. abstract a shared service.
Configuring behavior at build/deploy/runtime is realized by binding those choices as late as cost-effective.
A runtime kill switch binds the feature-enabled choice at runtime — the latest binding time.
Repointing to test data without code change relies on binding the concrete data source late (deploy/test time).
Swapping data sources requires an explicit abstracted interface that hides the concrete source.
Both inject controlled test conditions: substitute a data source and set/get/report internal state via test interfaces.
Control-and-observe testability: set/get/report/reset interfaces read and force the single localized state store.
Recorded interface state is restored into the localized state store to recreate a fault-inducing test state.
Assertions flag bad internal state; test interfaces expose/observe it — both control-and-observe testability tactics.
Assertions detect the moment state goes bad; record/playback replays the recorded state to reproduce that fault.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Testability ch., 'Limit Complexity' tactics
edges.note: The two limit-complexity tactics: cut structural complexity and remove nondeterminism to shrink what must be tested.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Testability ch., Limit Structural Complexity tactic
edges.note: Limiting structural complexity includes isolating and encapsulating environmental dependencies.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Testability ch., Limit Structural Complexity tactic
edges.note: Reducing inter-component coupling and breaking cyclic dependencies is how structural complexity is limited for test.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Testability ch., Limit Nondeterminism tactic
edges.note: Where nondeterminism is unavoidable, the tactic says to manage it with tactics like record/playback.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Usability ch., 'Support User Initiative' tactics
edges.note: User-initiative pair: cancel stops an in-progress action; undo reverses completed ones.
Both let the user interrupt a long-running operation and free its resources — pause defers, cancel terminates.
Support-user-initiative tactics that both hinge on preserving enough prior state to resume or to restore.
An aggregate operation on a selected group, and its undo, both apply to the whole group at once.
Support-user-initiative tactics acting on the user's current selection/operation: batch it, or cancel it mid-flight.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Usability ch., 'Support System Initiative' tactics
edges.note: System-initiative models combined: infer what the user is doing and who they are to assist them.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Usability ch., 'Support System Initiative' tactics
edges.note: System self-model plus task model together predict behavior and give context-aware feedback.
User model and system self-model together tune feedback (e.g., expected response time) to the specific user.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Integrability ch., 'Adapt' tactics
edges.note: Adapt tactics: tailor the interface (buffer/transform/mask) and configure behavior to fit the integrating system.
Tailoring adds/hides capabilities at an explicit interface boundary without touching the implementation.
Adhering to a standard interface plus tailoring adapters bridges an element into a standards-based ecosystem.
An orchestration engine is an interposed intermediary that sequences and invokes otherwise independent services.
A resource manager is an intermediary specialized to mediate access to shared computing resources.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Integrability ch., 'Coordinate' tactics
edges.note: Coordinate-integrability tactics: a resource manager mediates shared resources while an orchestrator sequences services.

edges.cite: Richardson, Microservices Patterns (2018), ch. 4 — saga orchestration vs. choreography
edges.note: Two ways to coordinate a multi-service workflow/saga: a central orchestrator vs. distributed choreography.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Integrability ch., 'Limit Dependencies' tactics
edges.note: Limit-dependencies integrability tactics: conform to shared standards vs. factor a shared abstract service.

edges.cite: Bass, Clements & Kazman, SAIP 4e, Deployability ch., Scale Rollouts tactic
edges.note: Gradual rollout monitors effects and rolls back the release if a problem appears.
Automated rollback executes the same scripted, version-controlled deployment commands to reach the prior state.
Scripted, tested deployment commands drive the ordered, coordinated steps of a gradual rollout.
To retract a bad feature: flip its runtime kill switch with no redeploy vs. roll the whole deployment back.
Feature flags gate a feature to user subsets and disable it instantly — complementing gradual/canary rollout.
Running multiple service versions simultaneously is what lets a rollout serve a new version to a subset while old serves the rest.
Manage-deployed-system tactics: version coexistence and per-feature toggles both expose or disable new behavior without redeploy.
Immutable, self-contained packaged versions make rollback a clean revert to the prior image.
Deployment scripts build and ship the packaged element-plus-dependencies as one consistent versioned unit.
